title: Unified Retail Inventory Analytics
business: Large-scale retail enterprises requiring real-time inventory visibility across disparate global supply chain systems.
problem: Data silos between legacy on-premises warehouse management systems and cloud-based e-commerce platforms prevent unified inventory reporting, leading to stock discrepancies.
solution: Azure Synapse Analytics integrates data warehousing and Spark-based processing to ingest, transform, and query heterogeneous data sources within a single workspace.
steps: Provision an Azure Synapse workspace to serve as the central analytics hub.
Configure linked services to connect to legacy SQL databases and cloud-based data lakes.
Utilize Synapse pipelines to orchestrate the movement and integration of raw inventory data.
Deploy Spark pools to perform complex data cleansing and normalization of disparate inventory schemas.
Expose the processed data via serverless SQL endpoints for consumption by business intelligence tools.
outcome: A unified, consistent view of global inventory levels that enables accurate demand forecasting and reduces stock-out incidents.
limitation: The primary limitation is the complexity of managing resource allocation between dedicated SQL pools and Spark pools; users must monitor pool utilization to ensure cost-effective query performance.

questions.question: In Unified Retail Inventory Analytics, what is the primary problem addressed by the solution?
options: Data silos between legacy and cloud systems causing inventory discrepancies
High latency in network connectivity between global warehouses
Lack of specialized hardware for on-premises database hosting
Inability to purchase third-party inventory management software
questions.explanation: The scenario explicitly identifies data silos between legacy and cloud systems as the cause of inventory discrepancies.
questions.evidence: Data silos between legacy on-premises warehouse management systems and cloud-based e-commerce platforms prevent unified inventory reporting, leading to stock discrepancies.

questions.question: In Unified Retail Inventory Analytics, what is a key limitation of the implementation?
options: The inability to connect to cloud-based data lakes
The requirement to manually code all data integration pipelines in Python
The complexity of managing resource allocation between SQL and Spark pools
The lack of support for serverless SQL endpoints
questions.explanation: Managing the balance of resources between different compute engines is a noted operational tradeoff.
questions.evidence: The primary limitation is the complexity of managing resource allocation between dedicated SQL pools and Spark pools; users must monitor pool utilization to ensure cost-effective query performance.
